speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the nature of your vertigo, specifically whether the room feels like it is spinning around you or if you feel like you are swaying?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the vertigo recur or worsen with specific head movements, such as rolling over in bed or looking up? I also need to know if you have any history of hearing loss, ringing in the ears, or ear fullness.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you experience any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or a feeling of fullness in one ear during the episode? Also, do you have any risk factors for stroke, such as high blood pressure, diabetes, or a history of smoking?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you currently have any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or a feeling of fullness in one ear? Also, are you experiencing any neurological symptoms like double vision, slurred speech, or weakness in your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies headaches, hearing loss, tinnitus, loss of consciousness or neurological deficits.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the vertigo is brief, triggered by position, and lacks auditory or neurological symptoms, I suspect Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo. Let me perform a physical exam to confirm. REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike Manoeuvre

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Positive, inducing nystagmus and reproducing patient’s symptoms of vertigo when head is turned to the left and laid back.

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver confirms the diagnosis of Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo. DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo
